used.text: Specification of Communication Management AUTOSAR AP R25-11 [SWS_CM_11272] Lifecycle management of FVM Upstream requirements: RS_CM_00801 ⌈ The lifecycle of an SecOC FreshnessValueManager implementation shall be man- aged by ara::com. ⌋ [SWS_CM_11273] Initialization of the FVM Upstream requirements: RS_CM_00801 ⌈ • The SecOC FreshnessValueManager implementation shall be initialized by calling Freshness Value Management Library API apext::com:: secoc::FVM::Initialize . ⌋ [SWS_CM_11274] SecOC secure channel sending Upstream requirements: RS_CM_00801, RS_CM_00802 ⌈ If a message is configured to be SecOC sent, the message shall be secured according to [29] and following steps shall be performed: • the message shall be handled as Authentic message by the Communication Man- agement • the message Authentication shall be performed in the order of operations after the E2E protection calculations • if the ServiceInterfaceElementSecureComConfig has an attribute freshnessValueId defined, the Communication Management shall call the Freshness Value Mananement Library API apext::com::secoc:: FVM::GetTxFreshness with the freshnessValueId • calculate the MAC using the Authentic message ([PRS_SecOc_00200] see [29]), (optionally the Freshness Value), and the dataId • if the attribute authInfoTxLength is defined, the Authenticator ([PRS_- SecOc_00210] see [29]) shall be truncated • if the attribute freshnessValueTxLength is defined, the Freshness Value shall be truncated ([PRS_SecOc_00103] see [29]) • combine the Authentic message, (truncated) Freshness Value , and (trun- cated) Authenticator ([PRS_SecOc_00211] see [29]) • continue in the Communication Management with the send processing The details for the construction of secure message are described in: [PRS_SecOc_ 00103], [PRS_SecOc_00105], [PRS_SecOc_00200], [PRS_SecOc_00208], [PRS_- SecOc_00210], [PRS_SecOc_00211] (see [29]) ⌋ 224 of 675 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement

Specification of Communication Management AUTOSAR AP R25-11 Then the error code ComErrc::kFieldValueNotInitialized shall be returned in the result type of OfferService() . ⌋ [SWS_CM_00129] Ensuring the existence of SetHandler Upstream requirements: RS_CM_00218 ⌈ Upon a call to OfferService() in a skeleton implementation for a given service, the following error check shall be made: if for at least one contained Field having hasSetter = true no SetHandler (see [SWS_CM_00116]) has been registered yet, the error code ComErrc::kFieldSetHandlerNotSet shall be returned in the result type of OfferService() . ⌋ [SWS_CM_00826] Minimum send interval time monitoring for SetHandlers calls by the client ⌈ To protect receivers from flooding/overload, each Set() of the respec- tive field class shall have a configurable Minimum Send Interval (see ServiceInter- faceDeploymentElement . minimumSendInterval ), which specifies the minimum amount of time that shall pass between two consecutive calls of SetHandlers by the client, i.e., the minimum send interval limits the maximum Tx frequency of a given Set() call for a Field in the network. If the application tries to Field::Set() a field value, by invoking Set() of the respective field class, ara::com shall check, whether the time since the last successful handover of the Set() call the underlying transmis- sion layer is greater than the specified Minimum Send Interval, i.e., the Minimum Send Interval is not violated. If the Set() handler has never been invoked before, this shall also successfully pass the minimum send interval check. If the Minimum Send Interval is not violated, ara::com shall process the Field::Set() call by handing it over to the transmission layer. The time of handover shall count as start of the new min- imum send interval monitoring. If the Minimum Send Interval is violated, ara::com shall discard the Field::Set() call, and return the error code ComErrc::kMini- mumSendIntervalViolationError (see [SWS_CM_10432]) shall be returned via the ara::core::Future of the Set() of the respective field class. The Minimum Send Interval shall only be check on the client side, i.e., by the instance that actually in- vokes the Field::Set() call and not by the server/provider, which responds/answers the Field::Set() call. If the configured Minimum Send Interval ( ServiceInter- faceDeploymentElement . minimumSendInterval ) of a Set() of the respective field class has the value 0, the Minimum Send Interval monitoring shall not be active for the corresponding Field::Set() . ⌋ [SWS_CM_00827] Default value of Minimum Send Interval and disabling Min- imum Send Interval time monitoring for SetHandlers for Clients ⌈ If the config- ured Minimum Send Interval ( ServiceInterfaceDeploymentElement . minimum- SendInterval ) of a Set() of the respective field class has the value 0, the Minimum Send Interval monitoring shall not be active for the corresponding Field::Set() , i.e., ara::com will not limit the Tx frequency by dropping Field::Set() calls by 288 of 675 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement
